parsed.main_gap: The subset-sum pigeonhole count in (11) is incorrect, though it is repaired by including the empty and full subset sums.

errors.description: From 2^{n+1}-2 points in (0,1), the average consecutive gap is less than 1/(2^{n+1}-3), not necessarily at most 1/(2^{n+1}-1). Include all 2^{n+1} subset sums, including 0 and 1; their 2^{n+1}-1 gaps sum to 1, giving the required bound, and the endpoint cases fit the subsequent argument.
errors.quote:
They lie in $(0,1)$, so their $2^{n+1}-3$ consecutive gaps sum to less than $1$. When put in nondecreasing order, two consecutive subset sums therefore differ by at most
\[
\frac1{2^{n+1}-1}=d.
\]

parsed.notes: Apart from this readily repairable pigeonhole error, the game-value reduction, pairing lemma, refinement construction, graph lower bound, and final strategy form a coherent and rigorous proof.
